## Bonchon (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/bonchon/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/bonchon.json
id: bonchon
aliases: Bonchon Chicken · 본촌치킨 · Bonchon International Inc.
said: Korean 본촌, pronounced roughly pon-chon; the company translates it as "my hometown".
facets: state=TX · status=open · founded=2002 · cooked=double-fried · styles=korean-american
region: Korean America, Texas, The United States
what: A Korean fried chicken chain that fries each piece twice and paints the sauce on with a brush. Jinduk Seo opened the first Bonchon in Busan, South Korea in 2002; the company now runs about 500 restaurants in more than ten countries and territories, keeps its global headquarters in Dallas, and manufactures every sauce in South Korea. Two sauces carry the brand: soy garlic and spicy. The chain closed its own South Korean restaurants at the end of 2016 and has exported ever since.
story: Bonchon began in the Busan chimaek trade — fried chicken eaten with beer — and built a double-fry meant to render fat out of the skin and leave a thin shell behind. Seo's own account of the moment it worked, on the company's site: "When police were dispatched to manage traffic around the new restaurant, I knew we had a winning formula."

The United States came next, through Fort Lee, New Jersey, and then twenty other states. Southeast Asia came by master franchise: the Scotland Food Group took the Philippines in 2010 and built 180 restaurants there; Minor International runs over 110 in Thailand. The home market went the other way. Facing saturation, the company shut its South Korean retail operations by the end of 2016 and turned itself into a pure export franchise, which makes it the first Korean fried chicken brand to expand internationally.

VIG Partners, a South Korean private equity firm, bought 55 percent for 60 billion won in December 2018, and the founding family kept 45. Headquarters moved to Dallas in 2021. In March 2026 VIG put the brand up for auction through William Blair; more than 100 buyers from the United States and Asia looked, and analysts valued the business at 3,000 billion won.

The chain has drawn criticism it has not always answered. Bonchon in South Korea, with the wider fried chicken trade, was accused of shrinkflation — smaller birds at higher prices — after which South Korean chicken restaurants were required to tell customers the pre-cooking weight. The Thai arm dropped a mandatory 10 percent service charge in 2024 after complaints. In October 2019 Bonchon paid more than $10,000 in back wages, tips and damages to former workers at the Dinkytown restaurant by the University of Minnesota, settling with the Minneapolis Labor Standards Enforcement Division a dispute over tips reassigned to kitchen staff.
how: Three steps, in the company's own words on bonchon.com, read 16 September 2026: hand battered in "a thin layer of flour and other secret ingredients", double-fried — "Once to lock in all the succulent juices and again to achieve that signature, crave-worthy crunch" — and hand brushed, because "We carefully brush every nook and cranny of that crunchy exterior… We do not drown our wings in sauce." Soy garlic uses Daseo-jong garlic; spicy uses dried gochugaru. Sauces are made at the South Korean plant and shipped to every franchise, which is how the chain holds one taste across every market. Pickled radish, kimchi and Korean street corn come alongside.
today: About 500 restaurants across North America, Asia, the Middle East, Oceania and Europe, the densest markets being the Philippines at 180, the United States at more than 150 and Thailand at over 110. The United States makes more than 60 percent of worldwide revenue. Newer restaurants run fast-casual — counter service, shorter menu, smaller footprint — beside ghost kitchens, hotels and airports.
address: Dallas, TX
geo: 32.7762719, -96.7968559 (town)
- kin → korean-american (style): The chain that carried the style out of Korea first, and the one many Americans meet it through.
- kin → double-fry (fry): Built the business on it: once to hold the juice, once for the shell.
- kin → soy-garlic-sauce (sauce): One of the two founding sauces, made with Daseo-jong garlic in South Korea and shipped worldwide.
- kin → yangnyeom-sauce (sauce): On the menu beside soy garlic, and made at the same South Korean plant.
- kin → the-toss (fry): Refuses it — the sauce goes on with a brush, in the company's words, rather than in a bowl.
- kin → pickled-radish (dish): Comes with the chicken, cold and sweet against the fry.
- kin → wingstop (place): Runs out of the same city, Dallas, on the opposite method: fried once and tossed, against fried twice and brushed.
- kin → extra-crispy (term): Sells the idea as a whole business: the second fry is what the word is asking for.
sources: s:wp-bonchon-chicken — Bonchon Chicken; s:web-bonchon-our-story — Our Story; s:web-bonchon-site — Korean Fried Chicken & Korean Food Restaurant | Bonchon; s:wp-korean-fried-chicken — Korean fried chicken

## Buffalo Wild Wings (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/buffalo-wild-wings/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/buffalo-wild-wings.json
id: buffalo-wild-wings
aliases: Buffalo Wild Wings & Weck · BW3 · BDubs · BWW
said: Regulars say B-Dubs. The older nickname, BW3, counts the three words of the original name: Buffalo Wild Wings & Weck.
facets: state=GA · status=open · founded=1982 · cooked=fried · styles=buffalo
region: The Ohio Valley, The United States
what: A sports-bar chain that put a Buffalo wing on a menu in Columbus, Ohio in 1982 and then on menus in all fifty states. Jim Disbrow and Scott Lowery opened it beside Ohio State University after failing to find Buffalo-style wings in Ohio. Wings go out in a long list of sauces and dry rubs — the chain's own sauce page counted 26 of them on 16 September 2026 — and the room is built around televised sport. Inspire Brands has owned it since 2018 and runs it from a support center in Sandy Springs, Georgia, which takes an Atlanta mailing address.
story: Jim Disbrow finished judging a figure-skating competition at Kent State in 1982, went looking for the wings he had eaten in Buffalo, and found none. He and Scott Lowery opened Buffalo Wild Wings & Weck near Ohio State in Columbus instead. The weck was beef on weck, the Buffalo sandwich they served alongside; it left the name later, and the wings stayed.

Growth came in bursts and nearly stopped once. Six more locations followed in Ohio, Indiana and Steamboat Springs. Franchising started in 1992 through a Chicago law firm, at a fee of $15,000 to $20,000 plus a share of sales. In late 1994 Disbrow hired a part-time chief financial officer, Sally Smith, and to get her full-time moved the company to Minnesota; Smith found lenders, the Internal Revenue Service and a possible bankruptcy waiting, and could not work out whether the company had made or lost money before 1995. That year it took $12 million and lost $1.6 million. Smith became president and chief executive in August 1996.

The chain reached its own namesake city late. Location 100 opened in Apple Valley, Minnesota in October 1999. Only in 2000, at 140 locations across 19 states, did one open in Buffalo, New York. Shares began trading on NASDAQ in November 2003. Disbrow died in October 2002.

Roark Capital Group and The Wendy's Company bought the chain for about $2.4 billion plus debt in a deal completed on 5 February 2018; Arby's Restaurant Group was renamed Inspire Brands and became the parent. Canada opened in 2010 and closed for good in June 2023.
how: Bone-in wings fry and then go into a sauce or a dry seasoning, chosen off a board arranged by heat. The company's sauces page, read on 16 September 2026, describes "26 Signature Sauces & Dry Rubs", the hottest of them Blazin'. Boneless wings are made from breast meat. Bottled versions of the sauces have sold through grocery since the 1990s, when the company upgraded the packaging to push home sales.
today: Over 1,300 locations across all fifty US states as of March 2025, run out of the Sandy Springs, Georgia support center by Inspire Brands, which also owns Arby's, Dunkin', Jimmy John's, Baskin-Robbins and Sonic. *Inference —* the sauce board, not the fry, is what the chain exports: a reader in Tucson picks Asian Zing or Nashville Hot off the same list as a reader in Buffalo.
address: Three Glenlake Parkway NE, Atlanta, GA, 30328
geo: 33.9353992, -84.3599421 (street)
- kin → jim-disbrow (person): Could not find a Buffalo wing in Ohio in 1982, so he opened this.
- kin → beef-on-weck (dish): The Weck in the original name — the Buffalo sandwich that shared the first menu and then left it.
- kin → buffalo (style): Took the style out of western New York on a franchise, and reached Buffalo itself only in 2000.
- kin → mango-habanero (sauce): One of the sauces off the board, and an argument about heat that a chain menu made national.
- kin → boneless-wings (dish): Sells them made from breast meat, beside the bone-in ones, on the same sauce list.
- kin → hooters (place): Opened a year later, on the same wing and a different sell.
- kin → wingstop (place): The counter-and-app chain that grew faster on a shorter menu, twelve years younger.
- kin → super-bowl-sunday (event): A sports bar on the biggest sports day of the American year.
- kin → the-price-of-a-wing (story): 1,300 kitchens buying the same cut is one reason the wholesale price moves.
sources: s:wp-buffalo-wild-wings — Buffalo Wild Wings; s:wp-buffalo-wing — Buffalo wing; s:web-bww-sauces — Buffalo Wild Wings Sauces, Dry Rubs and Flavors; s:web-inspire-contact — Contact — Global Support Center; s:web-buffalowing-hall-of-flame — Hall of Flame

## Capital City Mambo Sauce (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/capital-city-mambo-sauce/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/capital-city-mambo-sauce.json
id: capital-city-mambo-sauce
aliases: Capital City · Capital City, LLC
facets: state=MD · status=open · founded=2011
region: Washington, D.C.
what: A bottler, not a counter. Arsha and Charles Jones started Capital City in a home kitchen in 2011 to put D.C. mambo sauce in a jar, and the company now runs a headquarters and distribution building at Melford Town Center in Bowie, Maryland. The bottles reach Giant, Safeway, Wegmans and Target.
story: Capital City, LLC was established in 2011. The company says it was created "to give a taste of home to Washington, D.C. metropolitan natives" — Arsha Jones, a Washington native, made the sauce in her kitchen, and the family turned it into a business. Its own about page calls it "a minority, family-owned company" based in Arnold, Maryland.

Its history page puts the sauce's origin at Wings-n-Things, "an African American-owned restaurant," whose first shop it places at 7th and Florida Avenue NW in the late 1960s, where mambo sauce was made as a condiment for fried chicken wings. That account is one side of a long argument. The Mumbo trademark belongs to a Chicago line: Argia B. Collins Sr. used it from at least 1950, his successor Select Brands registered it in 1999, and the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board found a D.C. company could not take the name from its Chicago founder.

Charles Jones died in October 2019, aged 45 or 46 by different counts; Arsha Jones has run the company since. In 2017 the founders took Black Enterprise's Family Business award.

On 18 May 2021 the company signed for 8,280 square feet at 5021 Howerton Way in Melford Town Center, Bowie, moving its corporate headquarters and distribution out of a smaller Anne Arundel County warehouse. That address is why this bottler has a place record at all: it is a building a reader could drive to, not a shop they can eat in.
today: Bottled mambo sauce sells through national grocery. The company's own about page still names Arnold, Maryland as its base, while the 2021 lease named Bowie; this record maps the Bowie building and flags the disagreement.
address: 5021 Howerton Way, Bowie, MD, 20715
geo: 38.9566003, -76.7054417 (street)
- kin → mumbo-sauce (sauce): Bottles it, and publishes the D.C. origin story that the Chicago trademark holder disputes.
- kin → dc-mumbo (style): Took the style out of the carryout window and onto a supermarket shelf.
- kin → argia-b-collins (person): The Chicago sauce maker whose Mumbo trademark beat a D.C. claim to the name at the Trademark Trial and Appeal Board.
- kin → yums-carry-out (place): One of the D.C. carryouts this company's own history names as making its own version.
- kin → john-young (person): Sold wings under mumbo sauce in Buffalo in the early 1960s and pointed at a Washington restaurant for it, which is the chronology this company's account has to sit beside.
- kin → hot-sauce-labels (art): A label that had to put a city on a jar before a supermarket would stock it.
- kin → mumbo (term): Spells it mambo, which is the other half of the word's own argument.

## Central BBQ (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/central-bbq/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/central-bbq.json
id: central-bbq
aliases: Central Barbecue · CBQ
facets: state=TN · status=open · founded=2002 · cooked=smoked · styles=memphis-dry-rub, smoked-bbq-wing
region: Memphis
what: A Memphis barbecue house started in 2002 by two competition cooks, Craig Blondis and Roger Sapp, on Central Avenue. Smoked hot wings come off the same pit as the ribs, whole, in six finishes: wet, naked, jerked, dry spice, honey gold or sweet heat. The house line is "Smoke is Our Sauce."
story: Blondis and Sapp met on the barbecue circuit in the mid-1980s and competed at Memphis in May's World Championship Barbecue Cooking Contest before they went into business together. The pit at the first Central BBQ, on Central Avenue, was fired in 2002.

The method the house publishes: premium meats rubbed with a dry spice combination, marinated twenty-four hours, then smoked low and slow over hickory and pecan. In their words, "We live in the hardwood capital of the world and use hickory and pecan woods, along with our intricate dry rub and a whole lot of patience."

Blondis recorded an oral history with the Southern Foodways Alliance on 13 July 2008, interviewed by Rien T. Fertel for the Tennessee BBQ project. He described bringing competition-style barbecue to a Memphis storefront, a sauce board that includes vinegar and mustard styles uncommon in the city, and a kitchen run light: "if you can control consistency and quality, you will have repeat customers."

*Inference —* the wing here is a barbecue-counter wing, not a fryer wing. Where a Buffalo bar fries and then tosses, this pit smokes and then decides — and one of the six choices, naked, is to decide nothing.
how: Smoked, whole, then finished six ways: wet, naked, jerked, dry spice, honey gold or sweet heat. The dry spice is the house rub, the same one that goes on the ribs.
today: Four Memphis rooms in September 2026, including the Central Avenue original at 2249 Central Avenue, phone (901) 754-2216, plus Summer Avenue, Poplar Avenue and a downtown shop on East Butler Avenue. Smoked Hot Wings are on the menu at each.
address: 2249 Central Avenue, Memphis, TN, 38104
geo: 35.1258836, -89.9867443 (street)
- kin → smoked-bbq-wing (style): Runs the wing through a rib pit first, then decides whether to sauce it at all.
- kin → memphis-dry-rub (style): Puts the rib rub on the wing as one of six finishes, under the name dry spice.
- kin → memphis-rub (sauce): The house dry spice: a combination the kitchen keeps, applied before a twenty-four-hour marinate.
- kin → smoke-then-fry (fry): Stops at the smoke; this pit does not finish a wing in oil.
- kin → naked (term): One of the six wing finishes, and here it means no sauce rather than no breading.
- kin → jerk-marinade (sauce): Jerked is one of the six, on a Memphis pit rather than a Caribbean grill.
- kin → chings-hot-wings (place): The other Memphis wing in this set, fried and counted rather than smoked.
- kin → southern-foodways-alliance (org): Recorded Craig Blondis here in 2008 for its Tennessee BBQ project.

## Chickie's & Pete's (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/chickie-and-petes/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/chickie-and-petes.json
id: chickie-and-petes
aliases: Chickie's and Pete's
facets: state=PA · status=open · founded=1977 · cooked=fried · styles=buffalo, smoked-bbq-wing
region: Philadelphia
what: A Philadelphia sports bar and crab house that began as a Mayfair taproom in 1977 and now runs stadium, casino and airport rooms. Crabfries are what it is known for; Chickie's Wings come classic in six or ten, boneless in eight or twelve, in buffalo, sweet heat, dry rub or barbecue, with celery and blue cheese or ranch.
story: Peter and Henrietta Ciarrocchi ran a deli and in 1977 bought a small neighbourhood taproom called Wally's, at 4010 Robbins Avenue in Mayfair, northeast Philadelphia. Peter made three changes: he put stools at a standing-only bar, he ended the men-only rule, and he named the place for himself and his wife, whom everybody called Chickie.

Peter died in 1987 and his son Pete took it on. The Crabfries came from him — crinkle-cut fries dusted with a crab-boil spice blend and served with a warm white cheese sauce, no crab meat in them — and by 2008 the company counted five million orders sold. It trademarked "crab fries" in 2007 and sued over the phrase in 2011; one defendant settled out of court in August 2012. In February 2014 the company agreed to pay $8.5 million to settle a Department of Labor investigation and an employee suit over wage and hour law.

The expansion ran through stadiums: a building near Veterans Stadium in 1998, then Lincoln Financial Field, two casinos, and four rooms at Philadelphia International Airport. ESPN voted it the number one sports bar in North America in 2011.

*Inference —* the wing here is a sports-bar wing, and the sports bar is the point. Philadelphia's loudest wing institution was a radio eating contest rather than a fryer; this is where the same city went to sit down.
today: Seven locations across Philadelphia and southern New Jersey as of 2023: Robbins Avenue and Roosevelt Boulevard in Philadelphia, Lincoln Financial Field in South Philadelphia, Parx Casino in Bensalem Township, the Tropicana in Atlantic City, Bordentown and Egg Harbor Township. The wing board in September 2026 reads buffalo, sweet heat, dry rub or barbecue, classic or boneless.
address: 4010 Robbins Avenue, Philadelphia, PA, 19135
geo: 40.0274043, -75.0599741 (street)
- kin → wing-bowl (event): The other Philadelphia wing institution: a radio eating contest, held across town, that this bar is not part of.
- kin → boneless-wings (dish): Sold here alongside the classic, in eights and twelves, on the same board and at the same counts.
- kin → french-fries (dish): Its own version, Crabfries, carries a trademark the company has sued to defend.
- kin → buffalo (style): One of four finishes on the wing board, in a room that sells crab first.
- kin → celery-and-carrots (dish): Still on the plate here, with blue cheese or ranch, four hundred miles from Buffalo.
- kin → ranch-vs-blue-cheese (story): Puts the question on the menu and lets the order settle it.
- kin → super-bowl-sunday (event): A stadium-and-casino wing operation, which is what that day is built on.
- kin → the-price-of-a-wing (story): An $8.5 million wage settlement in 2014 is part of what a cheap bar wing has cost somebody.

what: A Memphis wing shop on Getwell Road, trading since 2003, selling whole wings by the piece from three to four hundred. Flavours run dry — Seasoned, Lemon Pepper, Dry Hot — and wet, through honey gold, hot, extra hot and one called Suicide. The house combination is the Kam Special: three dry seasonings with a honey hot drizzle over the top.
story: The shop dates itself to 2003 and credits its seasonings and sauces to its founder, whom its own pages do not name. It sits at 1264 Getwell Road in Memphis, and it closes two days a week.

Wings come whole — not split into flat and drum — and are ordered by count. In September 2026 three whole wings ran $8.25 and a four-hundred-piece party order of party wings ran $532.00.

The seasoning board reads as two arguments in one column. Dry Hot and Lemon Pepper belong to the Memphis rib-counter habit of putting seasoning on and stopping there; Honey Gold, Honey Hot and Suicide belong to the sauced wing. The Kam Special refuses to choose: dry seasonings first, then a drizzle.

*Inference —* the honey gold family on this board is close kin to what a Baltimore or a D.C. counter would call a sweet sauce, and the naming is local rather than national. The project has not found a source tracing that line, so it stays an observation about a menu.

## Country Sweet Chicken & Ribs (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/country-sweet-chicken-and-ribs/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/country-sweet-chicken-and-ribs.json
id: country-sweet-chicken-and-ribs
aliases: Country Sweet
facets: state=NY · status=open · founded=1977 · cooked=fried · styles=rochester-breaded
region: Rochester
what: A Rochester counter open since 1977, hand-breading its wings and glazing them in a sauce the founder built in a home kitchen and the city now buys by the bottle. The house says the sauce is "not quite BBQ, and it certainly wasn't Buffalo—it was something entirely new," which is the whole of Rochester's case against Buffalo in one line of its own marketing.
story: Tom Lask "created a sauce that defied categorization in a Rochester home kitchen" and opened Country Sweet in 1977, seventy miles east of the city that had just started exporting the cayenne-and-butter wing.

The sauce is sweet and tangy with heat behind it, sold in three grades: mild, hot, and a barbecue version the house calls "sweet and smokey with tang." It goes on wings that are breaded before they fry — "hand-breaded & crispy," in the house's own words, "classic wings tossed in Country Sweet glaze." Buffalo fries its wings naked and sauces them after; Rochester puts a coat on first and glazes the coat. Both cities call the result a wing and neither concedes anything.

The bottled sauce outgrew the counter. It sells in Rochester groceries, which means a Country Sweet wing is something a household makes as well as something a counter sells.
how: Wings are hand-breaded, fried, then tossed in the glaze rather than a thin sauce; a glaze clings and sets where a butter sauce runs. Ribs come off the same sauce.
today: The original counter at 1691 Mt Hope Avenue is open seven days as of September 2026 — Monday to Thursday 11am to 9pm, Friday and Saturday 11am to 10pm, Sunday noon to 9pm. A second room trades in Greece.
address: 1691 Mt Hope Avenue, Rochester, NY, 14620
geo: 43.1171914, -77.6219256 (street)
- kin → rochester-breaded (style): One of the counters the style is named for: coat first, fry, then glaze.
- kin → breaded-fry (fry): Hand-breads every wing before it goes in the oil.
- kin → buffalo (style): Seventy miles from it and declining both its sauce and its bare fry.
- kin → honey-bbq-sauce (sauce): The nearest national relative to a Country Sweet glaze, and the house says it is not that either.
- kin → jeremiahs-tavern (place): The other Rochester wing room, frying bare and tossing where this one breads and glazes.
- kin → garbage-plate (dish): Shares a city and a habit: Rochester puts sauce on top of everything and names it after the sauce.

## Duff's Famous Wings (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/duffs-famous-wings/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/duffs-famous-wings.json
id: duffs-famous-wings
aliases: Duff's · Duff's Sheridan Drive
facets: state=NY · status=open · founded=1946 · cooked=double-fried · styles=buffalo
region: Western New York
what: A wing house at Sheridan Drive and Millersport Highway in Amherst, north of Buffalo, open under that corner since 1946 and selling wings since 1969. Eight heat levels run from mild to death, and the house warns at every level that its scale runs hotter than the word suggests. Buffalo's long argument over who started the wing puts Duff's on the other side of it from the Anchor Bar.
story: Louise Duffney opened a corner gin mill at Sheridan Drive and Millersport Highway in 1946. The house dates its first wings to 1969: "It was in 1969 that the local tavern known simply as Duff's served up their first batch of chicken wings. Selling nearly 20 pounds of wings a week." Around 1985 the sign caught up with the trade and the name became Duff's Famous Wings.

That 1969 date does work in the origin argument. The Anchor Bar dates the Buffalo wing to 4 March 1964, but a local newspaper piece about the Anchor Bar in 1969 does not mention wings, and Duff's started selling them across town that same year.

The heat scale is the other thing people know. Visit Buffalo puts it plainly: "Order the medium sauce and you'll receive hot wings. Order hot wings, and you might give your tongue first-degree burns." The Buffalo sauce runs at eight levels, mild through death.
how: Wings arrive fresh, not frozen — the house specifies "roaster sized wings that are delivered daily" — and go out double-fried, sauced in recipes the house dates to 1969. Heat is picked at the order, and the printed warning does the rest.
today: The Sheridan Drive room still trades on its original corner. Wikipedia counts five Buffalo-area rooms, one in Rochester, one in Southlake, Texas, and three around Toronto; the company's own site lists ten across New York, Texas, Florida and Kentucky as of September 2026. A version of the wings went into Ralph Wilson Stadium in 2014 under a deal with the Buffalo Bills.
address: 3651 Sheridan Drive, Amherst, NY, 14226
geo: 42.9791498, -78.7983599 (street)
- kin → anchor-bar (place): Claims the wing against this house; a 1969 paper wrote the Anchor Bar up without mentioning wings, the year Duff's started selling them.
- kin → buffalo (style): Cooks the style, and its heat scale is where visitors learn the style's words don't mean what they say.
- kin → the-origin-fight (story): Holds the 1969 end of the argument, with a date and a receipt rather than a story.
- kin → double-fry (fry): Its wings go through the fryer twice, which is where the crust comes from.
- kin → buffalo-sauce (sauce): Bottles and pours it at eight heats, mild through death.
- kin → blue-cheese-dressing (sauce): Goes out beside the wings, and buys back some of the heat.
- kin → wingnutz (place): A newer neighbour just up the same highway, selling the same argument to a different decade.

## Elmo's Bar & Restaurant (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/elmos-bar-and-restaurant/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/elmos-bar-and-restaurant.json
id: elmos-bar-and-restaurant
aliases: Elmo's · Elmo's Restaurant & Bar
facets: state=NY · status=open · cooked=mixed · styles=buffalo
region: Western New York
what: A pitcher-and-television sports bar on Millersport Highway in Getzville, near the University at Buffalo's north campus, whose signature is a wing that goes through the fryer and then onto a grill. The Infatuation calls it the double dip. Orders arrive as sauce combinations — hot and barbecue, cajun and honey mustard — rather than a single heat.
story: Bon Appétit's Alex Delaney spent 2018 working through twelve Western New York wing rooms and ranked three. Elmo's came second, behind Gabriel's Gate and ahead of Mammoser's.

The double dip is what he was ranking. The Infatuation's David Neimanis, writing in February 2025, describes it: "Fried and sauced like usual, they're then coated in another layer of sauce and grilled, which locks in the smoky undertones while keeping the exterior delightfully crisp." Visit Buffalo's trail lists the combinations the second coat makes possible — "BBQ hot" and "Cajun honey mustard" among them.

Visit Buffalo records the room's other awards without naming years: it has been "rewarded with award winning wings and hamburgers from Gourmet magazine, The Buffalo News, and more."
how: Fry, sauce, sauce again, then grill. The second coat caramelises on the grill instead of sitting wet, which is the whole point of the method and the reason the order is named by two sauces rather than one heat.
today: Open Monday to Saturday as of September 2026, from 11:30am — noon on Saturday — and running to 2am most nights. Closed Sunday.
address: 2349 Millersport Highway, Getzville, NY, 14068
geo: 43.0141142, -78.768637 (street)

- kin → grill (fry): Uses one as a finishing step rather than a cooking one.
- kin → gabriels-gate (place): Beat this room in Bon Appétit's 2018 ranking with a plain fried wing and Frank's RedHot.
- kin → mammosers-tavern (place): Came third behind it in the same ranking.
- kin → the-pitcher (dish): The unit this room measures an evening in.
- kin → buffalo (style): Cooks the style and then adds a step the style does not have.

what: A restaurant and tavern at 145 Allen Street in Buffalo's Allentown, trading since 1969 inside an 1864 brick row house with tin ceilings and two wood-burning fireplaces. Wings go out big and crispy, sauced with Frank's RedHot, at heats the house runs "from mild to suicide-hot." Bon Appétit put them first in Buffalo in 2018, which is how a corner restaurant on a bar street acquired a line at the door.
story: The building came first. It is "one of the neighborhood's original Tift Row Houses, built in 1864"; the restaurant dates itself "Est. 1969."

In 2018 Bon Appétit's Alex Delaney worked through twelve Western New York wing rooms on camera and ranked three. Gabriel's Gate came first, Elmo's second, Mammoser's third. Visit Buffalo's trail describes what he was ranking as "the standard for a classic wing done right" — crisp, and sauced with Frank's RedHot rather than anything made in the building.
how: Fried, then sauced in Frank's RedHot at the heat asked for: the house line is "Big, crispy, juicy — sauces from mild to suicide-hot." The room keeps hardwood floors, wooden booths, saloon chandeliers and the fireplaces.
today: Open seven days as of September 2026, 11:30am to midnight Sunday through Thursday and to 1am Friday and Saturday. The house lists its awards as WNYers Choice wins — French onion soup, burgers, Reuben, mac and cheese, patio — none of them for the wings.
address: 145 Allen Street, Buffalo, NY, 14201

## Harold's Chicken Shack (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/harolds-chicken-shack/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/harolds-chicken-shack.json
id: harolds-chicken-shack
aliases: Harold's Chicken · Harold's · Harold's: The Fried Chicken King
facets: state=IL · status=open · founded=1950 · cooked=fried · styles=chicago-mild-sauce
region: Chicago
what: A Chicago fried-chicken institution founded by Harold Pierce in 1950 and franchised to friends and family, now past a hundred storefronts. The constants across the shops are the chicken dinners and the emblem of a cook chasing a chicken with a cleaver, often crowned; everything else — technique, seasoning, menu — varies shop to shop. The counter question is mild sauce or hot.
story: Harold P. Pierce was born 11 August 1917 in Midway, Alabama and came to Chicago in 1943, where he drove as a chauffeur. He and his wife Hilda ran a soul food restaurant on 39th Street called the H&H, whose specialities were dumplings and chicken feet. A friend, Gene Rosen, kept a poultry shop nearby and supplied the birds Pierce worked his recipe on.

Harold's Chicken Shack opened on 22 June 1950, at 47th Street on the South Side. The sources disagree about which corner: Wikipedia's article on the restaurant says 47th and Kenwood, near the estate where Pierce had worked; its article on Pierce says 47th and Greenwood. A 2026 Block Club Chicago piece reports 1235 East 47th Street and says the Greenwood corner came in 1962. This record puts the map pin at 1235 East 47th and leaves the argument open.

Pierce franchised the idea rather than standardising it. Franchisees bought their chickens from Rosen and were otherwise left alone, so technique, seasoning and menu vary shop to shop; the constants are the chicken dinners and the cook-and-cleaver emblem, sometimes in neon, sometimes hand-painted. Concentration on the South Side owes something to redlining, which limited where Pierce could expand. Some shops serve through bulletproof glass, which arrived as a necessity rather than a look.

Pierce retired in the early 1980s to Beaverville, Illinois, and raised hunting dogs. His second wife, Willa, took the business and expanded it beyond Chicago; she died on 21 January 2003. Pierce died on 8 March 1988 in Kankakee, Illinois, aged 70, of prostate cancer. Kristen Pierce, his daughter and the company's chief executive, died in January 2026.
how: *Tradition holds —* you order by number. The chicken is fried after the order goes in and dropped over fries, so the fries take the grease, with a slice of white bread on top. The counter question is mild sauce, hot sauce, both or neither. Mild sauce is the sweeter one, close to a barbecue sauce, that Harold's helped make standard on the South and West Sides.
today: As of 2025 the chain reported more than a hundred locations, about forty of them in Chicago, with clusters on the South Side and the southern suburbs, several on the West Side, western suburban shops in Oak Park and Aurora, a few on the North Side, and stores in Indiana, downstate Illinois, Arizona, Georgia, Nevada, Missouri, Texas, Minnesota, North Carolina and California. An Atlanta location opened in 2012 with a bar, as Harold's Chicken and Ice Bar; the Charlotte store carries a bar and hookah. The corporate picture is contested enough that Block Club Chicago ran a 2026 explainer on it, and this record does not try to settle who holds the name.
address: Chicago, IL
geo: 41.809569, -87.5959671 (street)
- kin → chicago-mild-sauce (style): One of the two counters Wikipedia credits with making mild sauce the South Side default.
- kin → mild-sauce (sauce): The question the counter asks before it hands the bag over.
- kin → harold-pierce (person): Founded it in 1950 and franchised it without standardising it, so no two shops fry quite alike.
- kin → uncle-remus-saucy-fried-chicken (place): The West Side counter Wikipedia names beside this one for mild sauce.
- kin → french-fries (dish): The chicken goes down on top of them, and they take the grease.
- kin → chicken-shack-signs (art): Carries the best-known one: a cook chasing a chicken with a cleaver, often crowned, in neon or hand paint.
- kin → argia-b-collins (person): The other Chicago sauce name of the same decades, and the trademark that the D.C. mumbo fight turned on.
- kin → boneless-wings (dish): Not the trade here: this counter sells the bird in bone-in pieces, wings among them.

## Hattie B's Hot Chicken (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/hattie-bs/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/hattie-bs.json
id: hattie-bs
aliases: Hattie B's
facets: state=TN · status=open · founded=2012 · cooked=fried · styles=nashville-hot
region: Nashville
what: A Nashville hot chicken house founded by a father and son both named Nick Bishop, open in Midtown since 2012 and now in seven cities. It is the one with a printed heat ladder, from Southern (no heat) up to Shut the Cluck Up, and it is where most people outside Nashville meet the dish.
story: The first Hattie B's opened in Midtown Nashville on 9 August 2012, at 112 19th Avenue South. The name comes from three women in the Bishop family, all called Hattie. The company is privately held and family owned.

The chicken is the Nashville preparation: fried, spiced, laid on white bread with pickles. What Hattie B's added was a written scale. Six steps are posted — Southern (No Heat), Mild, Medium, Hot!, Damn Hot!! and Shut the Cluck Up!!! — and the top one is built with ghost peppers.

Expansion followed the ladder. West Nashville in June 2014, Birmingham, Alabama in June 2016, a third Nashville shop in November 2017, Midtown Memphis in April 2018, Atlanta in July 2018, The Cosmopolitan in Las Vegas that autumn, Dallas in February 2022, and in 2026 a first Midwestern shop in Chicago's Wrigleyville, with Wicker Park and River North announced.

*Inference —* the argument this house draws is about what a heat ladder does to a dish. A printed scale makes the heat orderable by a stranger; at a shack it is a conversation with the counter. Both are Nashville hot chicken, and people will tell you at length which is which.
today: Columnists in USA Today and Sports Illustrated reviewed it in 2017, and The Daily Meal ranked it sixth that year among America's 75 Best Fried Chicken Spots. The Midtown room at 112 19th Avenue South still carries the queue.
address: 112 19th Avenue South, Nashville, TN, 37203
geo: 36.1514926, -86.7966244 (street)
- kin → nashville-hot (style): Carried the style out of Nashville to eight other cities, with the heat written down.
- kin → princes-hot-chicken-shack (place): The shack this house came after and is always measured against.
- kin → nashville-hot-oil (sauce): Built here in six graded strengths, the hottest with ghost pepper.
- kin → white-bread-and-pickles (dish): Kept from the shack preparation, under every order.
- kin → chicken-and-waffles (dish): On the menu beside the hot chicken, which a shack would not have carried.
- kin → boltons-spicy-chicken-and-fish (place): The East Nashville counter whose lowest heat is said to start where this one's top end sits.
- kin → atomic (term): The kind of word a heat ladder needs at the top; here it is Shut the Cluck Up.

provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

## Hooters (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/hooters/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/hooters.json
id: hooters
aliases: Hooters, Inc. · Original Hooters · Hooters of America
facets: state=FL · status=open · founded=1983 · cooked=fried · styles=buffalo
region: Florida, The United States
what: A restaurant chain that sells breaded wings, beer and a uniform. Six Clearwater, Florida businessmen incorporated Hooters, Inc. on 1 April 1983 and opened the first restaurant on 4 October that year at 2800 Gulf to Bay Boulevard, in a failed nightclub they bought cheap. Waiting staff are young women in a branded tank top and orange running shorts, called Hooters Girls, and the company has defended that hiring in court for thirty years. The wings come four ways: hand-breaded, naked, grilled in Daytona Beach sauce, or boneless.
story: The six founders — Lynn D. Stewart, Gil DiGiannantonio, Ed Droste, Billy Ranieri, Ken Wimmer and Dennis Johnson — picked April Fools' Day to incorporate because they expected to fail, and built a small graveyard of headstones at the door for the businesses that had died in the same building.

Control left Clearwater almost at once. Hugh Connerty bought the rights in December 1984; Robert H. Brooks and a group of Atlanta investors bought him out and built Hooters of America past 425 stores. Brooks died in 2006. Wellspring Capital, then Chanticleer Holdings and other investors in January 2011, then Nord Bay Capital and TriArtisan in July 2019 each took a turn owning it. The Clearwater company kept the Tampa Bay, Chicago and one Manhattan restaurant, the casino rights and the grocery sauces.

The uniform is the chain's documented controversy, and the record runs in two directions. Three men denied jobs in Orland Park, Illinois sued in 1997 and were awarded $19,100 each; four men in Maryland got $10,350 each. The settlement let Hooters keep hiring only women as waiting staff, and required other floor jobs — bartenders, hosts — to be filled without regard to gender. Hooters argues a bona fide occupational qualification: that the business is undermined if the policy goes. An older employee handbook, published by The Smoking Gun, had women sign that "The Hooters concept is based on female sex appeal and the work environment is one in which joking and entertaining conversations are commonplace." Four California chapters of the National Organization for Women complained to district attorneys in 2010 that the chain advertised itself as a family restaurant while defending its hiring on sex appeal, and asked authorities to make it choose. Hooters answers that it donates to charities promoting women's entrepreneurship, promotes Hooters Girls into management, and that 40 percent of its restaurant managers are women. Studies cited in the Wikipedia article associate the work with lower job satisfaction and higher anxiety; other writers argue that the choice of workplace is the woman's to make.

Other suits followed on other grounds. A federal jury awarded former Newport, Kentucky waitress Sara Steinhoff $275,000 in 2000 over unwanted advances and retaliation. Job applicants in West Covina, California were secretly filmed undressing in 2004. Farryn Johnson was awarded $250,000 in April 2015 after an arbitrator found race discrimination contributed to her firing over blonde highlights in her hair at the Baltimore restaurant. On 22 October 2024 Hooters of America paid $250,000 and signed a three-year consent decree to settle a US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission suit over a Greensboro, North Carolina restaurant that laid off about 43 people in the pandemic and recalled, the agency alleged, primarily white and lighter-skinned employees.

Sales fell from $1.2 billion in 2009 to $678 million in 2024. Hooters of America filed for Chapter 11 on 31 March 2025 with 305 restaurants worldwide. The Clearwater founders and a group of franchisees bought the Atlanta company on 14 October 2025 and said they would make the attire slightly more modest, end bikini nights, and return the brand to family-friendlier ground.
how: Hooters Original Style wings are breaded by hand and tossed in a chosen sauce; the chain's own menu page, read 16 September 2026, calls them "The style we invented over 40 years ago". Naked wings skip the breading. Daytona Beach style wings are naked, tossed in the Daytona sauce, then seared on a grill. Boneless wings are hand-breaded breast meat. Nearly every restaurant holds a beer and wine licence, and a full bar where the local permit allows.
today: The Clearwater founders' company, with Hoot Owl Restaurants LLC, finished buying Hooters of America on 14 October 2025 and controlled 140 of 198 US locations — about 200 restaurants and an estimated $700 million in system-wide sales, per Tampa Bay Business and Wealth on 3 November 2025. Closures continued through 2026: the last Long Island restaurant on 16 February, Mall of America on 22 March after 33 years, and by August 2026 every location in New York, Massachusetts, Connecticut and Minnesota, with notice given on a sheet of paper taped inside the door. A fast-casual spinoff called Hoots, launched 2017, drops the menu length and dresses servers of both sexes in t-shirts and khakis.
address: 2800 Gulf to Bay Boulevard, Clearwater, FL, 33759
geo: 27.9609583, -82.7212313 (street)
- kin → buffalo (style): Carried the style out of western New York on a franchise from 1983, breaded rather than bare.
- kin → breaded-fry (fry): Breads its house wing by hand, which is the older Rochester answer done at national scale.
- kin → naked (term): Prints the word on its own menu, as the option that skips the breading.
- kin → boneless-wings (dish): Sells hand-breaded breast meat under the wing heading, like most of the chains.
- kin → buffalo-wild-wings (place): Opened a year earlier in Columbus; the two chains carried the wing national together in the 1980s.
- kin → rochester-breaded (style): Shares the breading that Buffalo argues about, without sharing the city.
- kin → super-bowl-sunday (event): A wings-and-beer room on the day the wing count gets counted.
- kin → the-price-of-a-wing (story): Sales fell from $1.2 billion in 2009 to $678 million in 2024, and the wings kept costing what wings cost.
sources: s:wp-hooters — Hooters; s:wp-buffalo-wing — Buffalo wing; s:web-hooters-menu-wings — Wings; s:web-tbbw-hooters-2025 — Hooters' Clearwater-based founders regain full ownership of brand; s:web-eeoc-hooters-2024 — Hooters of America, LLC to Pay $250,000 to Settle EEOC Race and Color Lawsuit

## Horace & Dickie's Seafood (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/horaces-and-dickies/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/horaces-and-dickies.json
id: horaces-and-dickies
aliases: Horace and Dickie's · Horace & Dickies
facets: state=MD · status=open · founded=1990 · cooked=fried · styles=dc-mumbo
region: Washington, D.C.
what: A fried-fish carryout that ran thirty years at 12th and H Streets NE in Washington and now trades from Prince George's County, Maryland. Whiting on white or brown bread is the order it is known for; wings share the same fryer.
story: Richard "Dickie" Shannon opened the carryout on H Street NE in 1990 with a friend named Horace. The counter sold fried whiting as a sandwich or a dinner plate, with baked macaroni and cheese, collard greens, potato salad, candied yams, french fries, hush puppies, coleslaw, corn on the cob and seasoned potatoes beside it.

It closed on 1 March 2020. Shannon put it on the neighbourhood changing around him: "The customers here have been getting $100 tickets, $150 tickets, towed. And it's affected the business." He also said, flatly, "Gentrification is cultural genocide." He was 82 and said he would play more golf. A Takoma shop and a food truck kept running.

Shannon died of complications of COVID-19 on Sunday 6 February 2022, aged 84. His son Rasheed Black, the business manager, told WTOP: "I think people will remember him just making people laugh at the 12th Street location and here on Allentown Road." And: "The main thing that he did was he would basically give people second chances." His wife of thirty-two years, Nancy Shannon, said much the same to NBC4: "He gave everybody a chance. If they needed a job, even if they had a little blemish on their record, he would give them a chance." WTOP listed Camp Springs, Takoma Park, Glenarden and Waldorf as the shops carrying on.

*Inference —* the fish counter and the wing counter are the same counter in this city. A D.C. carryout fries whiting, wings and shrimp in the same oil and sends mumbo out with all three; that is why a seafood shop sits in a set about wings.
today: The Prince George's County tourism office lists the Camp Springs shop at 5601 Allentown Road, phone (301) 773-0140. *Tradition holds —* wings and wing dinners are on the board there; delivery listings carry them, and this project has not read a page from the business itself. No posted hours could be cited, so no day here is called open or closed.
address: 5601 Allentown Road, Camp Springs, MD, 20746
geo: 38.8108417, -76.8966754 (street)
- kin → dc-mumbo (style): A carryout of the style's own city, where the sauce reaches fish and wings out of the same fryer.
- kin → yums-carry-out (place): The other D.C. carryout in this set: wings and fried rice first, where this one is fish first.
- kin → mumbo-sauce (sauce): The bottle that travels down a D.C. counter like this one, whatever came out of the fryer.
- kin → french-fries (dish): On the sides board with hush puppies, yams and collards, and under the sauce if you ask.
- kin → wing-basket (dish): Sold here as a wing dinner: pieces, a side, bread.
- kin → the-price-of-a-wing (story): A counter that closed on rent and parking tickets rather than on the fryer, which is most of what the price of a wing means.
sources: s:web-dcist-horace-dickies — Horace And Dickie's Owner Says Gentrification Is Pushing Out His Fried Fish Carryout After 30 Years On H Street; s:web-wtop-dickie-shannon — Founder of DC-area's Horace and Dickie's Seafood dies at 84; s:web-nbc4-dickie-shannon — Owner of Horace & Dickie's Seafood Mourned in Maryland, DC; s:web-experience-pg-horace-dickies — Horace & Dickie's Seafood — listing

## J.R. Crickets (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/jr-cricketts/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/jr-cricketts.json
id: jr-cricketts
aliases: The Original J.R. Crickets · JR Cricket's
facets: state=GA · status=open · founded=1982 · cooked=fried · styles=atlanta-lemon-pepper, buffalo
region: Atlanta
what: A Midtown Atlanta wing bar open since 1982, founded by Paul Juliano, who still runs it. Its lemon pepper wet — medium wing sauce with dry lemon pepper shaken over the top — is the wing a television episode made famous, under a name the kitchen did not give it. The house line is “Chicken Is Chicken, but the Wing Is the Thing!”
story: Paul Juliano opened the Original J.R. Crickets in Midtown Atlanta in 1982; he is the founder and president, and CBS News Atlanta filmed him in the Midtown kitchen in 2026. *Tradition holds —* that Juliano came from Buffalo, New York, and gave the wings away by the sample because Atlanta had not met them yet. This project found that account only in press summaries it could not open directly, so it stays hedged here.

The lemon pepper wet order arrived sideways. *Tradition holds —* that a cook named the buffalo-and-lemon combination the Fester after what he thought of it, and that customers ordered the Fester as lemon pepper wet for years; the Atlanta press carries that account, and this project has it secondhand. Then the second episode of Donald Glover's FX series Atlanta put lemon pepper wet in a character's hands and named this restaurant. The writer Stephen Glover has said he wanted the character handed something that was not on the menu, and that the wing he pictured came from the American Deli. In 2017 J.R. Crickets put lemon pepper wet on its own menu under that name.

Juliano told CBS News Atlanta the house lemon pepper has “at least two items in it - ingredients - that nobody else uses.”
today: Thirteen locations were listed in September 2026, including the Midtown original at 129 North Avenue, stands inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium and State Farm Arena, and outposts in Tuscaloosa, Alabama and Fort Collins, Colorado. CBS News Atlanta reported the Midtown kitchen running about four thousand wings a day. In March 2026 an Atlanta Journal-Constitution blind tasting of eight finalists put J.R. Crickets first for lemon pepper.
address: 129 North Avenue NE, Atlanta, GA, 30308
geo: 33.7710457, -84.383192 (street)
- kin → atlanta-lemon-pepper (style): Put the city's wet version on a menu under that name in 2017, after customers had ordered it that way for years.
- kin → lemon-pepper-wet (sauce): Sold here as the Fester long before it was sold here as lemon pepper wet.
- kin → american-deli (place): The counter the show's writer says he actually had in mind when the wings went on screen here.
- kin → buffalo (style): Runs underneath the city's lemon pepper here: the wet order is a medium wing sauce with dry seasoning shaken over it.
- kin → blue-cheese-dressing (sauce): One of the two dips this bar puts beside a wing, against ranch, the way a Buffalo room would.
- kin → all-flats (term): The Atlanta order the 2 Chainz line fixed in place: twenty pieces, all flats, lemon pepper.
- kin → wet-and-dry (term): Two words that start every wing order at this counter.

## Jeremiah's Tavern (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/jeremiahs-tavern/

id: jeremiahs-tavern
aliases: Jeremiah's · Jeremiah's Monroe Ave
facets: state=NY · status=open · cooked=fried · styles=buffalo, rochester-breaded
region: Rochester
what: A tavern at 1104 Monroe Avenue in Rochester, the first of four rooms, frying wings that arrive "fresh, never frozen" in sauces the company mixes daily at its own commissary. The house claims a run of readers'-poll wins for wings longer than most of its staff have been alive. The Monroe Avenue kitchen also sells a plate, which is what Rochester calls the pile of meat and starch Nick Tahou Hots trademarked as the Garbage Plate.
story: Seventy miles east of Buffalo, Rochester breads its wings and Buffalo notices. Jeremiah's sits on the Buffalo side of that argument — fried, sauced, not battered — in a city that does not.

The house's claim is the streak: it says it has "been voted Rochester's Best Wings for 21 consecutive years as well as Best Family Friendly Restaurant and Sports Bar in Rochester." It does not name the poll. *Inference —* a twenty-one-year run in a city readers' poll is a claim about a ballot nobody else has to ratify, and this project records it as the house's own count rather than as a finding.

The Bee Sting is the house sauce people ask for by name; it turns up on the wings and then again on a chicken salad the menu trademarks.
how: Wings come in fresh and go in the fryer. Dressings and signature sauces are made daily at a commissary kitchen that supplies all four rooms, which is why the Bee Sting tastes the same in Greece as on Monroe Avenue.
today: Four rooms as of September 2026: Monroe Avenue in Rochester, Penfield at Fairport Nine Mile Road, Henrietta on Jefferson Road, and Greece at Paddy Creek Circle. Monroe Avenue runs Sunday to Wednesday 11am to 11pm with the kitchen closing at 10, and Thursday to Saturday 11am to midnight with the kitchen closing at 11.
address: 1104 Monroe Avenue, Rochester, NY, 14620
geo: 43.1389642, -77.5801464 (street)

## La Nova Pizzeria (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/la-nova-pizzeria/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/la-nova-pizzeria.json
id: la-nova-pizzeria
aliases: La Nova · La Nova Wings
facets: state=NY · status=open · founded=1957 · cooked=fried · styles=buffalo, smoked-bbq-wing
region: Western New York
what: A pizzeria on West Ferry Street in Buffalo's west side, run by three generations of the Todaro family, whose barbecue wing is the local counter-argument to cayenne and butter. The wings went from the pizzeria's own counter into a wholesale plant that ships them frozen across the country. Buffalo argues about whether a barbecue wing counts; La Nova sells them by the billion and does not enter the argument.
story: Joe Todaro — "Papa Joe" — opened La Nova in 1957 at 43 South Niagara Street in the City of Tonawanda, working the ovens with his son. Urban renewal shut that room after about a decade. The son, Joe Todaro Jr., "Big Joe," reopened on a corner in Buffalo: "Big Joe grew up with the business in his blood and opened La Nova Pizzeria on January 6, 1971." He is credited in the family's own telling with white pizza, steak and cheese subs, and the thing this record is here for: he "was also the first to create La Nova's World Famous Barbeque Wings; making them an absolute favorite in the Queen City."

The third generation took the wing out of Buffalo. Joey Todaro III first exhibited at the International Pizza Expo in 1994, selling pizzerias elsewhere on putting wings next to the pies; La Nova Wings, Inc. now calls itself "The Premier Manufacturer of Chicken Wings in the United States" and sells "fully cooked, heat and serve wings, boneless wings and sauces" in barbecue, oven-roasted, Italian-style and hot-and-spicy.

The family's other life is on the record too. Wikipedia's article on Joseph Todaro Jr. reports that a 1999 federal civil racketeering complaint named him as underboss and his father as boss of the Buffalo crime family and identified both as owners of La Nova Pizzeria, and that Canadian court proceedings in 2017 alleged he is the current boss. Todaro denied holding any leadership role in organized crime in a January 2023 interview.
how: Wings fry at the pizzeria and go out in the house barbecue sauce, oven-roasted, Italian-style or hot. The wholesale line cooks them fully and freezes them, so the same wing reaches a bar in another state as a reheat rather than a fry.
today: 371 West Ferry Street, open seven days as of September 2026: Sunday to Wednesday 10am to 10:15pm, Thursday to 11:15pm, Friday and Saturday to 12:15am. A second room trades at 5151 Main Street, Williamsville.
address: 371 West Ferry Street, Buffalo, NY, 14213
geo: 42.9151387, -78.8881731 (street)
- kin → honey-bbq-sauce (sauce): Its barbecue wing is the Buffalo argument against cayenne and butter, sold from a pizza counter.
- kin → buffalo-chicken-pizza (dish): Wings and pies come off one counter here, which is how the two ended up on the same menu everywhere else.
- kin → boneless-wings (dish): The wholesale line ships them frozen and fully cooked alongside the bone-in.
- kin → anchor-bar (place): A mile east, selling the other Buffalo sauce; both bottle and ship.
- kin → buffalo (style): Sits inside the style's home city and declines its sauce.
- kin → the-price-of-a-wing (story): Its plant is one reason a wing in another state costs what it costs.
- kin → smoked-bbq-wing (style): Put a barbecue wing on a Buffalo menu decades before the national chains did.

## Mammoser's Tavern & Restaurant (place)

id: mammosers-tavern
aliases: Mammoser's
facets: state=NY · status=open · cooked=fried · styles=buffalo
region: Western New York
what: A neighbourhood tavern on South Buffalo Street in Hamburg, twelve miles south of the city, pouring eighteen microbrew drafts and frying a wing in a house sauce built on four kinds of pepper. Bon Appétit put it third in Western New York in 2018. Closed Sundays.
story: Bon Appétit's Alex Delaney ranked three Western New York wing rooms on camera in 2018 after working through twelve. Gabriel's Gate came first, Elmo's second, Mammoser's third — a village tavern in the same sentence as two Buffalo rooms.

What Visit Buffalo's trail names is the pepper count: a homemade sauce "with four different varieties of pepper," delivering "a slow burn and extra kick." Slow burn is the argument. Buffalo's cayenne-and-butter sauce hits at the front of the mouth and leaves; a four-pepper sauce arrives late and stays, which is a different eating experience sold under the same word, hot.

The house describes itself as the room where "customers have been enjoying our famous wings for decades" and as "the friendly neighborhood bar that truly does know our customers by name." Listing sites date the tavern to 1947 and the building to a stable a century before that; this project could not read a page that states either, so both stay out of the record.
how: Fried, then sauced in the house's own four-pepper mix. Eighteen microbrew taps run alongside — Step Out Buffalo says it is "the only place in Hamburg, NY with 18 micro-brew drafts to choose from."
today: Monday to Saturday 11:30am to 11pm as of September 2026. Closed Sunday.
address: 16 South Buffalo Street, Hamburg, NY, 14075
geo: 42.7153208, -78.8292234 (street)

- kin → buffalo-sauce (sauce): Builds its version on four peppers, so the heat arrives late instead of at the front of the mouth.
- kin → gabriels-gate (place): Took first place over this room in Bon Appétit's 2018 ranking.

## Nine-Eleven Tavern (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/nine-eleven-tavern/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/nine-eleven-tavern.json
id: nine-eleven-tavern
aliases: The Nine-Eleven Tavern · 911 Tavern
facets: state=NY · status=open · founded=1981 · cooked=fried · styles=buffalo
region: Western New York
what: A cash-only corner tavern in South Buffalo, established 1981, whose wings come out large and heavily sauced in a recipe its late owner kept to himself. Buffalo Rising gives the address as 9-11 Bloomfield Avenue; the mailing address is 11. Five days a week, no cards, no delivery.
story: Mark Gress opened it in 1981. Buffalo Rising, writing in 2016, put it at “35 years” and called the payment policy in four words: “it's cash only.”

The name is the street number. *Inference —* the house does not print an explanation, but Buffalo Rising lists the address as “9-11 Bloomfield Avenue | Buffalo, NY 14220-1920”, two numbers for two rooms, and local press repeats that the tavern took its name from them. It is not named for Seneca Street and it is not named for the date; the tavern was nineteen years old by September 2001.

The sauce is the other closed subject. The Buffalo Wing Trail describes the result rather than the recipe: “large, crispy, and saucy” with a sauce that “starts sweet and tangy, then builds towards a robust, fiery finish.” Buffalo Rising's reviewer found “a nice vinegar to butter ratio” and his wife found the sauce “a bit on the sweeter side and were lacking in the heat department,” which is the argument in one sentence.
how: Fried, sauced heavily, served in the bar or the back room with the attached deck. Bottles of the house sauce sell over the counter. Cash.
today: Kitchen Tuesday to Thursday 4:30–9pm and Friday and Saturday 4:30–9:30pm; the bar runs half an hour to an hour longer. Closed Sunday and Monday. The house lists Buffalo Wing Coalition wins for 2025 and 2026 and a Buffalo Spree best-wings vote in 2013, and says Gress was inducted into the Buffalo Wing Hall of Flame.
address: 11 Bloomfield Avenue, Buffalo, NY, 14220
geo: 42.8452004, -78.8233371 (street)

## Peppa's Jerk Chicken (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/peppas-jerk-chicken/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/peppas-jerk-chicken.json
id: peppas-jerk-chicken
aliases: Peppa's · Peppa's Jerk Chicken Restaurant
facets: state=NY · status=open · founded=2005 · cooked=grilled · styles=caribbean-jerk
region: New York City, Caribbean America
what: A Jamaican takeout counter on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn's Little Caribbean, run by Gavin Hussey, whose jerk chicken is dry-rubbed, washed with vinegar and charred black before it is hacked apart to order. It stays open to six in the morning. A house scotch-bonnet jerk sauce goes over the top on request.
story: Hussey was born in St. Andrew Parish, Jamaica, third of twelve children, and learned to cook helping his mother feed the younger ones. The nickname Peppa goes back to school and, Black-Owned Brooklyn notes, has nothing to do with chiles.

In 1995 he co-founded a Flatbush Avenue counter called Danny & Pepper's, selling mostly jerk chicken. Ten years later he opened his own room on the same avenue. The Historic Districts Council, naming Peppa's to its Six to Celebrate list, says "his unique style of jerking made the restaurant a neighborhood favorite" and describes it as a staple of Little Caribbean. Two more Brooklyn rooms followed — Crown Heights run by his daughter, East Flatbush by his sister.

Hussey on the work, quoted by Black-Owned Brooklyn: "You can't cook just to sell some food. You have to put the passion in it to get it right — and that's who I am."

*Note —* this is a wing catalogue and jerk wings are a national item, but no menu this project could read lists wings at Peppa's. The record is here for the jerk method that the jerk wing descends from, not for a wing order.
how: A dry rub and a vinegar wash, then fire until the outside goes black, then the chicken is hacked up with a cleaver for serving. Scotch-bonnet jerk sauce over the top is separate. Time Out's phrase for the result is "the smokey, perfectly grilled smoked chicken that keeps us coming back."
today: Four rooms as of September 2026: the Flatbush Avenue original, Crown Heights at 791 Prospect Place, East Flatbush at 689 Utica Avenue, and one in Manhattan. Sources put the original at 730, 736 and 738 Flatbush Avenue — the same storefront, numbered differently by different listings.
address: 738 Flatbush Avenue, Brooklyn, NY, 11226
geo: 40.6549839, -73.9598946 (street)
- kin → caribbean-jerk (style): Cooks the method the jerk wing borrows: dry rub, vinegar wash, char, then the cleaver.
- kin → jerk-marinade (sauce): Works dry here — rub and wash rather than a wet soak — and the scotch-bonnet sauce goes on after.
- kin → mango-habanero (sauce): The bar-menu descendant of a scotch-bonnet sauce like the one poured here.
- kin → blondies-sports-bar (place): Both stay open past every other kitchen in this set, for opposite reasons.
- kin → grill (fry): The fire is the whole method here; nothing goes near a fryer.
- kin → nashville-hot (style): The other American style that puts its heat in a paste on the outside of the bird rather than in a sauce afterwards.

## Prince's Hot Chicken Shack (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/princes-hot-chicken-shack/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/princes-hot-chicken-shack.json
id: princes-hot-chicken-shack
aliases: Prince's Hot Chicken · Prince's Hot Chicken South · BBQ Chicken Shack
facets: state=TN · status=open · founded=1945 · cooked=fried · styles=nashville-hot
region: Nashville
what: The Nashville hot chicken shack, started by James Thornton Prince and run since 1980 by his great-niece André Prince Jeffries. Chicken — breast, thigh or wing — is marinated, floured, fried to order and painted with a cayenne paste, then served on white bread under pickle slices. Everybody else's hot chicken is measured against it.
story: The family story is that hot chicken began as revenge. Thornton Prince was, by the account his own family tells, a womanizer; after a late Saturday night a girlfriend cooked him fried chicken loaded with pepper. He liked it. He and his brothers built their own recipe and opened the Bar-B-Que Chicken Shack. Wikipedia gives 1945 for the business and says the current style of spice paste may only date to the mid-1970s, with spicy fried chicken in Nashville's Black neighbourhoods long before either.

The café started at 28th Avenue and Jefferson Street, then moved downtown into Hell's Half Acre near the Ryman Auditorium, where Opry stars came after the show. Under segregation the house built a separate room for white guests, who walked through the main dining room and the kitchen to reach it. In 1988 it moved to Ewing Drive in East Nashville.

When Thornton Prince died his brother Will took over; Will's wife Maude ran it after him. In 1980 Maude decided that Thornton's great-niece André Prince Jeffries should have it, and Jeffries dropped the BBQ out of the name.

In December 2018 a Ford Explorer drove into the strip mall holding the Ewing Drive shop and set it on fire. The restaurant itself was not damaged and Jeffries expected two weeks; damage to the building and the landlord's delays turned it into a permanent closure announced seven months later. That location had run since 1989.

Jeffries recorded an oral history with the Southern Foodways Alliance on 7 July 2006, for the Nashville Eats project: no advertising, word of mouth for eighteen years, three heats, chicken fried only after the order, a thirty-minute wait, and her own term for the aftermath, "24-hour chicken."
how: Marinate, flour, fry to order, then paste. The cayenne paste goes on with a spoon and gloves and is squeezed into the crust by hand. It lands on white bread with pickle chips, and the bread takes the grease and some of the heat.
today: Four locations in September 2026: Prince's Hot Chicken South at 5814 Nolensville Pike, a stall in Assembly Food Hall at 5055 Broadway, Tanger Outlets on Cane Ridge Parkway, and a counter at Nashville International Airport by the C/D concourse. A Jefferson Street shop is announced as coming.
address: 5814 Nolensville Pike, Nashville, TN, 37211
geo: 36.0438469, -86.7122145 (street)
- kin → nashville-hot (style): The shack the style is named out of, and the one every other hot chicken house is read against.
- kin → thornton-prince (person): Started it, and is the man in the revenge story the family still tells.
- kin → andre-prince-jeffries (person): Took it in 1980, when Maude — the widow of Thornton's brother Will — decided it should be hers, and dropped the BBQ from the name.
- kin → nashville-hot-oil (sauce): The cayenne paste that goes on after the fry, by spoon and glove, and is a closely held recipe.
- kin → white-bread-and-pickles (dish): What the chicken lands on, which is service and heat management at once.
- kin → hattie-bs (place): The 2012 Nashville house that carried this style to a wider room, with a printed heat ladder.
- kin → boltons-spicy-chicken-and-fish (place): Founded by the nephew of a cook who came up through these kitchens.
- kin → southern-foodways-alliance (org): Recorded André Prince Jeffries in 2006 and made a film about the shack.
- kin → buffalo (style): The other cayenne wing: sauce after the fry there too, but butter instead of paste, and celery instead of bread.
sources: s:wp-prince-s-hot-chicken-shack — Prince's Hot Chicken Shack; s:wp-hot-chicken — Hot chicken; s:web-sfa-princes — Prince's Hot Chicken Shack — oral history with André Prince Jeffries, Nashville Eats project; s:web-princes-locations — Locations — Prince's Hot Chicken
provenance default: cited · confidence: high · needs_verification: False · updated: 2026-09-16

region: Atlanta
what: A wing bar on Roswell Road in east Cobb County, outside Atlanta, carrying thirty-five to forty sauces and marinades and thirty to fifty beers on tap. It opened as a Wild Wing Cafe and kept trading under its own name after the chain link ended.
story: The room turned thirty in June 2025, which puts its opening around 1995, under the Wild Wing Café name. The Cobb County Courier wrote it up that month: a suburban wing bar with karaoke, trivia, music bingo, poker nights, weekend bands, seasonal crawfish boils, a covered patio that takes dogs and a tiki bar.

The sauce board is the point. The Courier counted more than thirty-five, naming Garlic Parmesan, Raspberry Chipotle BBQ, classic Buffalo, a General Tso's style, Smokin' Maple Bacon and a beer-built one called Endless Summer, with cilantro, garlic and lime.

*Inference —* the long-board format belongs to the 1990s casual wing bar rather than to any city's wing. Atlanta's own argument, lemon pepper wet against dry, is a two-item question; a forty-sauce board is a different proposition, and both are on the same road.
today: Open daily, at 2145 Roswell Road in Marietta, as the Cobb County Courier reported in June 2025.

## Uncle Remus Saucy Fried Chicken (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/uncle-remus-saucy-fried-chicken/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/uncle-remus-saucy-fried-chicken.json
id: uncle-remus-saucy-fried-chicken
aliases: Uncle Remus
facets: state=IL · status=open · founded=1963 · cooked=fried · styles=chicago-mild-sauce
region: Chicago
what: A West Side Chicago fried-chicken counter whose sauce is in its name. Gus W. Rickette Sr. and Mary F. Rickette started it in 1963 as the G & G Chicken Shack and renamed it Uncle Remus in 1969; their daughter Charmaine Rickette Alfred runs it now. The company calls itself "a Black-owned and women-led business with a rich history rooted in Chicago's West Side."
story: Gus and Mary Rickette came to Chicago from Mississippi and opened the G & G Chicken Shack in 1963. The Uncle Remus name went up in 1969: first at 210 South Cicero in February, then at 5611 West Madison Street in August, in Austin. The Cicero shop is gone. Broadview followed in June 2004, Bronzeville at 747 East 47th Street in June 2015, and a small counter at 26th and Wabash after that.

Wikipedia names Uncle Remus, alongside Harold's Chicken Shack and Lem's Bar-B-Q, among the South and West Side restaurants that made mild sauce popular. *Tradition holds —* Charmaine Rickette told Block Club Chicago in 2020 that her father began serving mild sauce in the 1960s after watching customers mix ketchup and hot sauce themselves, which is the recipe in two moves; this project has that account secondhand and marks it unverified.

*Inference —* the family tells the story as a migration story, Leland to Chicago, and the sauce sits inside it rather than beside it: the shop's name is a sauce adjective.

The brand also polices itself. Its own site lists the addresses it stands behind and says any similarly named business is not affiliated. The founding year is not settled between the family's own pages either: the story page dates the first shack to 1963 and the rename to 1969, while the brand's other site carries "The Original Since 1968."
today: Three official locations as of September 2026, per the company: 5611 West Madison Street in Chicago, 1801 Roosevelt Road in Broadview, and a cashless micro counter at 2537 South Wabash Avenue inside Picnic. The company's story page also lists the Bronzeville shop on East 47th Street, which the three-location page does not; this record does not resolve that.
address: 5611 West Madison Street, Chicago, IL, 60644
geo: 41.8800579, -87.7654004 (street)
- kin → chicago-mild-sauce (style): Carries the sauce in its own name — saucy fried chicken — and is named among its originators on the West Side.
- kin → mild-sauce (sauce): Started here in the 1960s, the family says, after customers were seen mixing ketchup and hot sauce themselves.
- kin → harolds-chicken-shack (place): The South Side counter Wikipedia names beside this one whenever mild sauce comes up.
- kin → mild-sauce-word (term): The word a Chicago counter says, which is not the same word a D.C. counter says for its own red sauce.
- kin → dc-mumbo (style): The other city's carryout sauce, and the other half of an argument about who made it first.
- kin → french-fries (dish): What the sauce goes over when it is not going over the chicken.
- kin → chicken-shack-signs (art): One of the West Side signboards the phrase Saucy Fried Chicken belongs to.

## Wingnutz (place)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/place/wingnutz/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/place/wingnutz.json
id: wingnutz
aliases: Wingnutz Bar & Grill · WingNutz Bar and Grill · Wingnutz Buffalo
facets: state=NY · status=open · founded=2005 · cooked=fried · styles=buffalo
region: Western New York
what: A sports bar on Millersport Highway in Williamsville, run by Ed and Alicia Wrazen, whose wings ran for thirteen years out of a Knights of Columbus hall before they had a restaurant. A podcast episode in 2021 turned a local following into an international one. The wings are large, crisp and sauced in mixes the couple make themselves.
story: The Wrazens started at home in 2005. Buffalo Rising's Mark Lazzara, writing in August 2019, traced "a 13-year journey" from home catering through cooking jobs to the Knights of Columbus hall on Kenmore Avenue, and reported that Yelp had counted Wingnutz "the best Chicken Wing Spot in the State of New York." His description of the product: "smothered in their homemade secret sauce, while so crisp."

The house's own account of why they started is short: "Our background begins a long time ago (2005), in a kitchen far away (our house). As our story begins, we were unemployed." They had been eating wings across Buffalo and had not found what they wanted.

In 2021 the hosts of Pardon My Take, a sports podcast the house says draws more than 750,000 listeners an episode, ate the Wrazens' wings and published the verdict as a title: "We Found The Best Wings In The World." Step Out Buffalo's Brett Llenos Smith, writing in January 2024, dates the full sports bar to after that: "After appearing on the popular Pardon My Take podcast in 2021, Ed and Alicia Wrazen turned to A.J. Giordano to take their Wingnutz restaurant to scale." The Millersport Highway room took over the former Santora's Pizza Pub & Grill space.
how: Fried, then sauced in house mixes. The signature is "sweet with a touch of tang"; the hot is "hot, yet bursting with flavor (and addictive!)". Step Out Buffalo's word for the wings themselves is "larger, juicier and crispier."
today: Three rooms in the Buffalo area as of September 2026: Millersport Highway in Williamsville, Genesee Street in Cheektowaga inside the Buffalo Airport Hotel, and a Lakeland location. The Millersport room posts Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday 11am to 10pm and Friday and Saturday 11am to 12:30am; Monday and Tuesday are not posted anywhere this project could read.
address: 1402 Millersport Highway, Williamsville, NY, 14221
geo: 42.9892342, -78.7914392 (street)
- kin → buffalo (style): Cooks the style, and started by eating everyone else's version of it and disagreeing.
- kin → duffs-famous-wings (place): Just up the same highway, sixty years older, arguing heat scale against size.
- kin → beef-on-weck (dish): Shares the menu, as it does at most Erie County wing rooms.
- kin → super-bowl-sunday (event): A sports bar built after a sports podcast; the calendar it lives on runs to February.
- kin → the-price-of-a-wing (story): Went from a hall kitchen to three rooms in three years, which is what a viral wing costs and earns.
- kin → anchor-bar (place): The room Wingnutz's founders were measuring themselves against when they started in 2005.
