## Neon chicken (art)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/art/neon-chicken/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/art/neon-chicken.json
id: neon-chicken
aliases: neon bird · neon chicken sign
facets: kind=neon
region: The United States
what: A chicken drawn in bent glass tube, filled with gas, and run off a transformer over a bar, a drive-in or a wing counter. The bird is usually animated in the cheap way neon animates: two or three sets of tubes switched in sequence so a wing flaps, steam rises, or an arrow chases. Neon signs are made by hand, by a bender working a ribbon burner, which is why a town's neon looks like the shops of the two or three benders who worked there. They are expensive to build, expensive to repair, and the first thing an owner replaces when a tube goes, which is why the surviving ones are mostly in cities that decided to protect them.
- kin → chicken-shack-signs (art): The unlit half of the same trade: same bird, paint instead of glass.
- kin → rooster-weathervanes (art): The same bird as a mark, three centuries earlier and driven by wind instead of current.
- kin → hot-sauce-labels (art): Shares the flame-and-glow vocabulary, shrunk to a bottle.
- kin → buffalo-murals (art): What replaced the big sign in cities that stopped permitting them.
- kin → elmos-bar-and-restaurant (place): A Buffalo-area bar of the type whose window neon is the whole of its street presence.
- kin → nine-eleven-tavern (place): A corner tavern whose door sign does the work a pole sign does elsewhere.
- kin → jr-cricketts (place): An Atlanta wing counter working the same after-dark hours neon was built for.
- kin → wing-night (term): The night the lit sign is selling; neon and the midweek special keep the same hours.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/images/neon-chicken/neon-chicken-chicken-in-the-rough-route-66-oklahoma.jpg · CC BY 2.0 · Jerry Huddleston · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AChicken_in_the_Rough%2C_Route_66%2C_Oklahoma.jpg

## Rooster weathervanes (art)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/art/rooster-weathervanes/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/art/rooster-weathervanes.json
id: rooster-weathervanes
aliases: weathercock · cockerel vane
facets: kind=mascot
region: The United States, New England
what: A rooster cut or moulded in sheet metal, balanced on a spindle, and put on a roof to show which way the wind blows. It is the oldest American use of a chicken as a public sign, it predates every wing counter by centuries, and the shape it settled into — flat body, raised comb, fanned tail, one leg forward — is the same silhouette a fried chicken sign draws today. American vanes were made in copper and zinc by nineteenth-century firms working from moulds, and museums now hold them as folk sculpture; the Smithsonian American Art Museum has released photographs of several under CC0.
- kin → chicken-shack-signs (art): Inherited the vane's silhouette, and its problem: a bird that has to read from far away.
- kin → neon-chicken (art): The same bird lit and hung at street level rather than balanced on a roof.
- kin → hot-sauce-labels (art): The same trick at bottle scale — an animal or a devil standing in for what is inside.
- kin → buffalo-murals (art): The largest version of the bird-as-mark, and the one with a copyright attached.
- kin → harolds-chicken-shack (place): A chain whose sign carries a drawn bird of exactly this descent.
- kin → wing (term): The part of the bird the vane makes its tail out of, and the part the menu sells.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/images/rooster-weathervanes/rooster-weathervanes-rooster-weathervane-saam-1992-12-3-1.jpg · CC0 1.0 · AnonymousUnknown author · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ARooster_Weathervane-saam-1992.12.3_1.jpg

## Wing festival posters (art)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/art/wing-festival-posters/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/art/wing-festival-posters.json
id: wing-festival-posters
aliases: Wing Fest poster art · wing contest promotional art
facets: kind=poster · state=NY
region: Western New York, Philadelphia, The United States
what: A wing festival poster does four things at once: names the event, fixes the date and the gate, lists the sponsors in descending size, and supplies a mascot the event can print on a T-shirt. The National Buffalo Wing Festival, founded in Buffalo in 2002 and held on Labor Day weekend, is the genre's anchor; Philadelphia's Wing Bowl, run by a radio station from 1993 to 2018, produced the same artwork in a louder register. The art is commercial, it is dated by design, and almost none of it is free to reuse — which is why this page describes it rather than shows it.
- kin → national-buffalo-wing-festival (event): The event whose annual artwork anchors this genre, running on Labor Day weekend since 2002.
- kin → drew-cerza (person): Founded the festival in 2002 and is the figure the poster's crown usually belongs to.
- kin → wing-bowl (event): Philadelphia's radio-built contest, whose promotional art borrowed from boxing rather than from food.
- kin → joey-chestnut (person): The competitor most often on the poster and in the photographs Commons actually holds.
- kin → national-chicken-wing-day (event): The other dated occasion the same artwork gets reused for.
- kin → chicken-shack-signs (art): Same trade, permanent instead of annual, and made by the same kind of local shop.
- kin → buffalo-murals (art): Where the festival's imagery ends up when a city wants it year-round.

- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/images/wing-festival-posters/wing-festival-posters-buffalo-wing-fest-crowd.jpg · CC0 1.0 · Fortunate4now · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ABuffalo_wing_fest_crowd.jpg
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/images/wing-festival-posters/wing-festival-posters-joey-chestnut-at-the-2012-national-buffalo-wing-fest-040edaf.jpg · CC BY 2.0 · LegendLarrys · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AJoey_Chestnut_at_the_2012_National_Buffalo_Wing_Festival%2C_Buffalo%2C_New_York.jpg

## Boneless is not a wing (story)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/story/boneless-is-not-a-wing/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/story/boneless-is-not-a-wing.json
id: boneless-is-not-a-wing
aliases: Berkheimer v. REKM · The boneless wing case
facets: kind=essay · state=OH
region: The United States, The Ohio Valley
what: On 25 July 2024 the Supreme Court of Ohio held, 4 to 3, that a diner who swallowed a chicken bone from a boneless wing could not take his negligence claim to a jury, because he could reasonably have guarded against it. The case is Berkheimer v. REKM, L.L.C., 2024-Ohio-2787, 177 Ohio St.3d 431, docket 2023-0293. The majority wrote that calling the item a boneless wing described a cooking style. The dissent called that reasoning jabberwocky, twice. The argument the case dropped into is older than the case and older than the menu category: a boneless wing is breast meat, battered and fried, and the federal standard that governs what may be labelled a wing does not cover a restaurant menu at all.
- kin → boneless (term): The word the court read as a cooking style and the dissent read as a promise.
- kin → boneless-wings (dish): The menu item itself: breast meat, floured, fried, sauced like a wing.
- kin → wing (term): The word the federal standard protects on a label and leaves unprotected on a menu.
- kin → flat (term): One of the two pieces a bone-in order actually contains, and the reason the count works differently.
- kin → breaded-fry (fry): How a boneless wing is built: coat the meat, batter the coat, fry it.
- kin → dredge (fry): The flour-and-spice step that makes a strip of breast hold a crust.
- kin → buffalo-wild-wings (place): Sells both, side by side, and prices them against each other.
- kin → wingstop (place): Carries boneless as a full parallel menu, sauced from the same list as bone-in.
- kin → the-price-of-a-wing (story): Why the category appeared: wing meat got dear and breast meat did not.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/images/boneless-is-not-a-wing/boneless-is-not-a-wing-buffalo-wings-at-concert-sarah-stierch.jpg · CC BY 4.0 · Sarah Stierch · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ABuffalo_Wings_at_Concert_-_Sarah_Stierch.jpg
sources: s:web-courtlistener-berkheimer — Berkheimer v. REKM, L.L.C. — case record (docket 2023-0293, 2024-Ohio-2787, 177 Ohio St.3d 431, filed 2024-07-25); s:web-volokh-boneless — Should Consumers Expect to Find Bones in "Boneless Wings"?; s:web-cbs-boneless-wings — Diners who order boneless chicken wings can't expect them to really be boneless, court rules; s:web-hklaw-boneless — Court Decision Concerning "Boneless Chicken Wings" Ignites Political Firestorm in Ohio; s:web-counter-boneless — Boneless chicken wings: It's not a lie if you believe it; s:web-ecfr-381-170 — 9 CFR 381.170 — Standards for kinds and classes, and for cuts of raw poultry; s:web-consumer-reports-wyngz — Stephen Colbert's right: wyngz rhetoric; s:web-thompson-coburn-wings — 'Boneless wings' or 'saucy nugs': Viral video provides lesson on food labeling laws; s:wp-chicken-nugget — Chicken nugget; s:wp-buffalo-wing — Buffalo wing

## Free to use (story)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/story/free-to-use/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/story/free-to-use.json
id: free-to-use
aliases: Sources and licences · What this project stands on
facets: kind=resources
region: The United States
what: Every map, price, coordinate and recipe on this site comes from somewhere a reader can go and check. This page names each archive, dataset, directory and licence, says what it is good for, says what it will not tell you, and names the ones this project could not get into. Licences are quoted from the publisher's own terms. Dates are the dates I read them, which for all of these is 16 September 2026.
- kin → the-price-of-a-wing (story): Built entirely out of the two USDA series described here, week and all.
- kin → boneless-is-not-a-wing (story): The story where a court record could not be fetched and reporting had to stand in for it.
- kin → the-origin-fight (story): What happens when the archives named here hold nothing: the argument runs on testimony.
- kin → ranch-vs-blue-cheese (story): Runs on the one public poll there is, because the scanner data is sold by subscription.
- kin → buffalo-wing-trail (org): A promoter's list of fourteen shops, recorded here as attention paid and not as a ranking.
- kin → national-chicken-council (org): Publishes the number every January and not the method behind it.
- kin → southern-foodways-alliance (org): Oral histories free to read, rights retained, permission required to reuse.
- kin → buffalo-murals (art): Why this site links to walls and does not reproduce them: the paint is somebody's copyright.

## Ranch against blue cheese (story)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/story/ranch-vs-blue-cheese/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/story/ranch-vs-blue-cheese.json
id: ranch-vs-blue-cheese
aliases: The dip argument
facets: kind=essay
region: The United States, Western New York
what: Buffalo sends out blue cheese. America buys ranch. Blue cheese reached the wing plate on the first night of the Anchor Bar story, off the antipasto tray, and it is still the house cup along the city's wing trail. Ranch was invented by a plumbing contractor named Steve Henson in the early 1950s, sold by mail from a Santa Barbara County guest ranch from 1957, bought by Clorox in 1972, and has outsold every other salad dressing in the United States since 1992. Asked what they eat wings with, more Americans say ranch than say blue cheese, by roughly two to one in the trade association's own polling. Both numbers and both dips are set out below, with whose figures they are and when they were taken.
- kin → blue-cheese-dressing (sauce): The dip Buffalo sends out unasked; it reached the plate off the Anchor Bar's antipasto tray.
- kin → ranch-dressing (sauce): Steve Henson's buttermilk dressing, best-selling in the United States since 1992 and the one most survey respondents name for wings.
- kin → buffalo (style): The style whose plate this argument is fought over.
- kin → celery-and-carrots (dish): Came out of the same antipasto tray as the blue cheese, and stayed for the same reason.
- kin → anchor-bar (place): Where the blue cheese cup enters the record, on the first night of its own story.
- kin → buffalo-wing-trail (org): Fourteen Buffalo-area stops, and the blue cheese cup is the house default at them.
- kin → wingstop (place): Makes ranch in the store every morning and sells it as a brand of its own.
- kin → national-chicken-council (org): Runs the Harris Poll that produces the ranch-versus-blue-cheese percentages everyone quotes.
- kin → buffalo-sauce (sauce): What the dip is set against: cayenne, vinegar and butter, which is why the dip is dairy and fat.
- kin → the-origin-fight (story): Same night, same tray — the blue cheese arrives in the story that nobody can document.

## The flat and the drum (story)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/story/the-flat-and-the-drum/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/story/the-flat-and-the-drum.json
id: the-flat-and-the-drum
aliases: Flats against drums
facets: kind=essay
region: The United States
what: A chicken wing has three joints and yields two pieces a kitchen will sell: the drumette, which is the humerus with the meat pushed to one end, and the flat, which is the two-boned middle section carrying most of the skin. The tip goes to stock. One bird gives one of each per wing, in a fixed ratio nobody can change, which is the whole economics of the argument: a counter can let you order all flats, but it cannot buy a bird that grows two of them. Federal regulation names the drumette and declines to name the flat. Survey respondents prefer the drum by a wide margin and split sharply by who is answering. No public price series prices one piece against the other.
- kin → wing (term): The whole limb this page takes apart, and the word that slid from the limb to its pieces.
- kin → flat (term): The two-boned middle piece, the one federal regulation refuses to name.
- kin → drumette (term): The humerus end, and the piece 45% of surveyed wing-eaters say they want.
- kin → wing-tip (term): The third segment, cut off and boiled, which is why a wing sells as two pieces and not three.
- kin → flapper (term): What the tip is called when a counter keeps it on the flat and sells it attached.
- kin → all-flats (term): The order this whole argument turns into money — the one request that leaves the kitchen holding something.
- kin → party-wing (term): What a grocery calls the pair once a processor has already split them.
- kin → wing-cut (fry): Where the knife goes, which decides everything on this page.
- kin → the-price-of-a-wing (story): The wholesale series quoted here in full, and what it did between 2021 and now.
- kin → naked-fry (fry): Why the flat's skin matters: bare in the oil, the skin is the whole of the crust.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/images/the-flat-and-the-drum/the-flat-and-the-drum-buffalo-wings-8779045398.jpg · CC BY 2.0 · Eugene Kim from San Francisco, USA · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ABuffalo_Wings_%288779045398%29.jpg
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/images/the-flat-and-the-drum/the-flat-and-the-drum-homemade-buffalo-wings.jpg · CC BY 2.0 · stef yau · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3AHomemade_buffalo_wings.jpg

## The origin fight (story)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/story/the-origin-fight/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/story/the-origin-fight.json
id: the-origin-fight
aliases: Who invented the Buffalo wing
facets: kind=essay · state=NY
region: Western New York, The United States
what: Two Buffalo kitchens claim the wing, and neither claim rests on a document. The Anchor Bar dates the dish to the night of 4 March 1964 and tells the story three different ways. John Young was selling breaded whole wings in a tomato sauce he called mumbo from 1961, registered his shop's name at the county courthouse, and said the Anchor Bar carried no wings as a regular menu item until 1974. A 1969 newspaper profile of the Anchor Bar does not mention wings. Duff's started selling them across town that same year. The city proclaimed a Chicken Wing Day in 1977, Calvin Trillin carried the story out of western New York in 1980, and the National Buffalo Wing Festival put John Young in its Hall of Flame in 2013. This page lays out who claims what and on what evidence.
- kin → buffalo (style): The style this argument is about; it takes its name from the city and not from either shop.
- kin → anchor-bar (place): Holds one side of it, dates it to 4 March 1964, and owns the trademark on the phrase.
- kin → john-young (person): Holds the other side, from 1961, with a breaded whole wing in mumbo sauce and a courthouse registration.
- kin → teressa-bellissimo (person): Fried the wings every Anchor Bar version turns on.
- kin → frank-bellissimo (person): Told the mistaken-delivery version, and took the city's 1977 proclamation.
- kin → dominic-bellissimo (person): Tended the bar that night and told the story to Calvin Trillin in 1980.
- kin → calvin-trillin (person): Wrote the 1980 New Yorker piece that carried the Anchor Bar version out of western New York.
- kin → duffs-famous-wings (place): Started selling wings in 1969, the year a paper profiled the Anchor Bar without mentioning them.
- kin → mumbo-sauce (sauce): What John Young put on his wings, which is why his dish and the Anchor Bar's are not the same dish.
- kin → national-buffalo-wing-festival (event): Put John Young in its Hall of Flame in 2013, forty-nine years after the Anchor Bar's date.
- kin → city-of-buffalo (org): Issued the 1977 proclamation, the oldest official paper in the argument.
- kin → buffalo-murals (art): Where Young's claim is held now: a wall at Jefferson and Carlton, put up in 2021.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/images/the-origin-fight/the-origin-fight-buffalo-wings-at-airport-anchor-bar.jpg · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Flickr user: Andrew Nash Vienna https://www.flickr.com/people/andynash/ · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ABuffalo_-_Wings_at_Airport_Anchor_Bar.jpg
sources: s:wp-buffalo-wing — Buffalo wing; s:wp-anchor-bar — Anchor Bar; s:wp-duff-s-famous-wings — Duff's Famous Wings; s:trillin-1980 — An Attempt to Compile a Short History of the Buffalo Chicken Wing; s:wp-calvin-trillin — Calvin Trillin; s:wp-national-buffalo-wing-festival — National Buffalo Wing Festival; s:wp-mumbo-sauce — Mumbo sauce; s:web-buffalorising-young-mural — A Banner Day for the Legacy of John Young, aka "King of the Wings"; s:web-visit-buffalo-wing-trail — Buffalo Wing Trail

## The price of a wing (story)
URL: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/story/the-price-of-a-wing/
JSON: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/api/story/the-price-of-a-wing.json
id: the-price-of-a-wing
aliases: What a wing costs
facets: kind=essay
region: The United States
what: In 1964 the wing was the cheapest thing on the bird, which is the premise every origin story rests on. In the week of 7 to 11 September 2026 it traded wholesale at 110.02 cents a pound, twice the price of a drumstick and ten times the price of the backs and necks that the Anchor Bar story says were supposed to arrive instead. It has been dearer than that: 325 cents a pound in May 2021, when cold storage ran to its lowest level since 2012. Every figure on this page carries its date and whose figure it is, and the ones I could not get are named too.
- kin → wing (term): The cut whose price this page tracks, from throwaway to 110 cents a pound.
- kin → the-flat-and-the-drum (story): Why no series prices one piece against the other: the wholesale line is Wings – Whole and nothing finer.
- kin → boneless-is-not-a-wing (story): The menu category the 2018 price inversion built, and which outlived it.
- kin → national-chicken-council (org): Publishes the Wing Report every January; a producers' trade association, which is worth knowing when reading the number.
- kin → super-bowl-sunday (event): The single day the whole industry's headline number is built around.
- kin → wing-night (term): What a bar does when the cut is cheap, and stops doing when it is not.
- kin → anchor-bar (place): Its third origin version has backs and necks arriving as wings by mistake; in 2026 that mistake costs ten times the order.
- kin → party-wing (term): How the grocery sells it, and the line USDA's retail report actually prices.
- kin → wingstop (place): Built a national chain on the cut during the years it was cheap.
- image: https://nanobotco.github.io/buffalo-wings/images/the-price-of-a-wing/the-price-of-a-wing-buffalo-wings-6676460575.jpg · CC BY 2.0 · Charli Lopez from Rochester, USA · https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File%3ABuffalo_Wings_%286676460575%29.jpg
